scenes.title: ACID
scenes.narration: ACID is the set of four guarantees that make relational transactions trustworthy even when systems crash or many users work at once.

scenes.title: The four guarantees
bullets: Atomicity: a transaction is all-or-nothing, never half applied
Consistency: every transaction moves the database from one valid state to another
Isolation: concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one at a time
Durability: once committed, changes survive crashes and power loss
scenes.narration: ACID stands for four properties. Atomicity means a transaction either fully succeeds or fully fails, never leaving half its work behind. Consistency means every transaction respects the database's rules and moves it from one valid state to another. Isolation means concurrent transactions do not corrupt each other and appear to run serially. Durability means once you commit, the change is permanent even if the server loses power a moment later.

scenes.title: Atomicity in practice: a money transfer
scenes.narration: This transfer moves a hundred dollars between two accounts. The two updates are wrapped in a single transaction started by BEGIN. Atomicity guarantees we can never debit one account without crediting the other. If both statements succeed we call COMMIT and the change becomes permanent. If either fails, ROLLBACK discards both updates so money is never lost or duplicated.

scenes.title: How durability survives a crash
steps: Change is written to the write-ahead log (WAL) on disk first
COMMIT is acknowledged only after the log entry is flushed
Data pages may be updated in memory and written later
After a crash, the log is replayed to restore committed changes
scenes.narration: Durability relies on the write-ahead log. Before a commit is acknowledged, the change is recorded in the log and flushed to disk. The actual data pages can be updated in memory and written to their final location later, which keeps things fast. If the server crashes, on restart the database replays the log, redoing every committed change so nothing is lost.

scenes.text: ACID is what lets you trust that a payment either fully happened or fully did not. Without these guarantees, concurrency and failures would silently corrupt your data.
scenes.narration: The payoff of ACID is trust: a payment either completes entirely or not at all, and committed data endures. Without these guarantees, ordinary concurrency and crashes would quietly corrupt your records.
